issues.description: Resolver postcondition (prepared=True, needs_more_preparation=False) silently retired without a restated owner.
issues.detail: The resolver previously guaranteed every requirement was fully prepared on return. The patch deletes that loop without stating who now owns the invariant; each command must remember to call prepare_linked_requirements_more, and future callers will be wrong by default. Restate the postcondition explicitly or centralize the transition.

issues.description: set_dist/get_dist precedence is undocumented and may shadow a fully-prepared distribution.
issues.detail: get_dist now returns self._distribution before metadata_directory or local_file_path with no stated invariant. A cached metadata-only BaseDistribution can shadow a later-materialized real dist after full preparation, silently handing callers a stale metadata-only view. Either document the precedence, clear _distribution on full prepare, or split into distinct metadata vs installed accessors.

issues.description: download_info is set as a side effect of the metadata-only fetch with unstated preconditions on source_dir.
issues.detail: When _fetch_metadata_only succeeds, the caller mutates req.download_info via direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir), but source_dir may be unset in metadata-only mode. The contract for None source_dir and the absence of a hash are not justified, risking malformed DirectUrl output in pip lock / --report. Compute download_info at link time as a pure function of the link.

issues.description: Three command modules duplicate the same prepare_linked_requirements_more call site.
issues.detail: download.py, install.py, and wheel.py each independently invoke prepare_linked_requirements_more after resolve(), duplicating logic the resolver used to own. This is incidental complexity migrated into every caller; the next command added will forget the call. Introduce a single finalize-resolution helper or a lazy dist accessor that triggers preparation on demand.

issues.description: No test demonstrates that --dry-run actually avoids the wheel download or that pip lock emits correct download_info.
issues.detail: The news fragment claims dry-run no longer downloads full wheels and that lock/report still work, but the diff adds no regression test asserting the network/cache is not hit on a PEP-658 metadata path, nor that download_info is well-formed from metadata-only fetches. The load-bearing new behavior is unverified and will silently regress.

issues.description: InstallRequirement remains a mutable place accumulating phase state instead of being modeled as a sequence of values.
issues.detail: The patch threads another flag (cached _distribution) through an already place-oriented InstallRequirement that tracks metadata_directory, download_info, needs_more_preparation, and prepared across phases. The right shape is immutable values: ResolvedLink -> MetadataOnlyReq -> FullyPreparedReq. Without that separation, every new phase will produce another shadowing bug.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch achieves a desirable behavior — no full-wheel download under --dry-run when PEP 658 metadata exists — but does so by silently retiring a resolver postcondition and scattering its restoration across three command modules. The new set_dist/get_dist precedence and the side-effect assignment of download_info from a possibly-unset source_dir both rest on preconditions the author has not articulated. No regression test exercises the load-bearing new behavior. The change is plausibly correct but under-specified and under-tested; restate the invariants, centralize the finalization step, and add tests before landing.
